claim: Type Ib synapses have relatively low Pr and facilitate in response to high-frequency stimulation.
source: Type Ib synapses have relatively low Pr and facilitate, whereas type Is synapses have higher Pr and depress in response to high-frequency stimulation (Aponte-Santiago et al., 2020; Lnenicka and Keshishian, 2000).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work (Aponte-Santiago et al., 2020; Lnenicka and Keshishian, 2000).

claim: Type Is synapses have higher Pr and depress in response to high-frequency stimulation.
source: Type Ib synapses have relatively low Pr and facilitate, whereas type Is synapses have higher Pr and depress in response to high-frequency stimulation (Aponte-Santiago et al., 2020; Lnenicka and Keshishian, 2000).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work (Aponte-Santiago et al., 2020; Lnenicka and Keshishian, 2000).

claim: Individual synapses formed by both low- and high-Pr inputs exhibit heterogeneous release properties that can be predicted by VGCC abundance alone.
source: We find that individual synapses formed by both low- and high-Pr inputs exhibit heterogeneous release properties that can be predicted by VGCC abundance alone.
evidence: Supported by functional imaging data showing correlation between Cac levels and Pr at individual synapses (Figure 1E, F).

claim: VGCC abundance does not correspond to differences in Pr between type Ib and type Is inputs.
source: However, VGCC abundance does not correspond to differences in Pr between the two inputs.
evidence: Supported by confocal imaging data showing similar average Cac levels at type Ib and Is AZs (Figure 1G, H).

claim: The same number of VGCCs are more densely organized at high-Pr synapses.
source: We find that the same number of VGCCs are more densely organized at high-Pr synapses, consistent with tighter VGCC-synaptic vesicle coupling.
evidence: Supported by STORM imaging data showing higher VGCC density at type Is AZs (Figure 2H, I).

claim: The α2δ–3 subunit Straightjacket is less abundant at high-Pr type Is inputs.
source: We generated endogenously tagged lines to investigate VGCC subunits in vivo and found that the α2δ–3 subunit Straightjacket along with the CAST/ELKS active zone (AZ) protein Bruchpilot, both key regulators of VGCCs, are less abundant at high-Pr inputs, yet positively correlate with Pr among synapses formed by either input.
evidence: Supported by confocal imaging data of endogenously tagged StjV5-N (Figure 6F).

claim: Bruchpilot is less abundant at high-Pr type Is inputs.
source: We generated endogenously tagged lines to investigate VGCC subunits in vivo and found that the α2δ–3 subunit Straightjacket along with the CAST/ELKS active zone (AZ) protein Bruchpilot, both key regulators of VGCCs, are less abundant at high-Pr inputs, yet positively correlate with Pr among synapses formed by either input.
evidence: Supported by confocal imaging data showing lower Brp levels at type Is AZs (Figure 3B).

claim: Straightjacket levels positively correlate with Pr among synapses formed by either type Ib or type Is input.
source: We generated endogenously tagged lines to investigate VGCC subunits in vivo and found that the α2δ–3 subunit Straightjacket along with the CAST/ELKS active zone (AZ) protein Bruchpilot, both key regulators of VGCCs, are less abundant at high-Pr inputs, yet positively correlate with Pr among synapses formed by either input.
evidence: Inferred from the positive correlation between Stj and Cac levels at individual AZs (Figure 6G, H) combined with the positive correlation between Cac and Pr (Figure 1E, F).

claim: Bruchpilot levels positively correlate with Pr among synapses formed by either type Ib or type Is input.
source: We generated endogenously tagged lines to investigate VGCC subunits in vivo and found that the α2δ–3 subunit Straightjacket along with the CAST/ELKS active zone (AZ) protein Bruchpilot, both key regulators of VGCCs, are less abundant at high-Pr inputs, yet positively correlate with Pr among synapses formed by either input.
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work showing Brp levels positively correlate with Pr at type Ib AZs (Gratz et al., 2019; Muhammad et al., 2015; Newman et al., 2017; Peled et al., 2014; Reddy-Alla et al., 2017) and data showing Brp and Cac levels strongly correlate at type Is AZs (Figure 3D).

claim: Both Straightjacket and Bruchpilot levels are dynamically increased across AZs of both inputs when neurotransmitter release is potentiated following glutamate receptor inhibition.
source: Consistently, both Straightjacket and Bruchpilot levels are dynamically increased across AZs of both inputs when neurotransmitter release is potentiated to maintain stable communication following glutamate receptor inhibition.
evidence: Supported by confocal imaging data showing increased Brp and Cac levels at both type Ib and Is AZs following PhTx treatment (Figure 4C, D) and increased Stj levels following PhTx treatment (Figure 7C).

claim: Cacophony is the sole Cav2 pore-forming subunit in Drosophila.
source: In Drosophila, Cacophony (Cac) is the sole Cav2 pore-forming subunit and is the VGCC responsible for triggering synaptic transmission (Kawasaki et al., 2000; Macleod et al., 2006; Peng and Wu, 2007; Smith et al., 1996).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work (Kawasaki et al., 2000; Macleod et al., 2006; Peng and Wu, 2007; Smith et al., 1996).

claim: Cacophony is the VGCC responsible for triggering synaptic transmission in Drosophila.
source: In Drosophila, Cacophony (Cac) is the sole Cav2 pore-forming subunit and is the VGCC responsible for triggering synaptic transmission (Kawasaki et al., 2000; Macleod et al., 2006; Peng and Wu, 2007; Smith et al., 1996).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work (Kawasaki et al., 2000; Macleod et al., 2006; Peng and Wu, 2007; Smith et al., 1996).

claim: Type Is synapses exhibit significant heterogeneity in Pr.
source: As has been previously reported, we found that type Is synapses exhibited significant heterogeneity and higher average Pr than type Ib synapses (Figure 1B and C; Lu et al., 2016; Newman et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by functional imaging data (Figure 1B, C) and citations to prior work (Lu et al., 2016; Newman et al., 2022).

claim: Type Is synapses have higher average Pr than type Ib synapses.
source: As has been previously reported, we found that type Is synapses exhibited significant heterogeneity and higher average Pr than type Ib synapses (Figure 1B and C; Lu et al., 2016; Newman et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by functional imaging data (Figure 1B, C) and citations to prior work (Lu et al., 2016; Newman et al., 2022).

claim: Type Is connections contain relatively fewer low-Pr and more high-Pr AZs compared to type Ib.
source: Consistent with their higher Pr, type Is connections contain relatively fewer low-Pr and more high-Pr AZs (Figure 1D).
evidence: Supported by functional imaging data showing quintile distribution of single-AZ Pr frequency (Figure 1D).

claim: At type Is inputs, single-AZ Cac intensity positively correlates with Pr.
source: We next investigated the correlation between Pr and VGCC levels and found that at type Is inputs, single-AZ Cac intensity positively correlates with Pr (Figure 1E).
evidence: Supported by functional imaging data showing correlation between CacTd-Tomato-N intensity and Pr at type Is AZs (Figure 1E).

claim: At type Ib inputs, single-AZ Cac intensity positively correlates with Pr.
source: We also observe a strong positive correlation between VGCC levels and Pr at type Ib inputs to the same muscles (Figure 1F), consistent with our and others' prior findings (Akbergenova et al., 2018; Gratz et al., 2019; Newman et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by functional imaging data (Figure 1F) and citations to prior work (Akbergenova et al., 2018; Gratz et al., 2019; Newman et al., 2022).

claim: Average Cac levels are the same at type Ib and Is AZs.
source: We analyzed CacsfGFP-N levels at individual type Ib and Is synapses and found that average Cac levels are the same at type Ib and Is AZs (Figure 1G and H).
evidence: Supported by confocal imaging data showing no significant difference in CacsfGFP-N AZ intensity between type Ib and Is terminals (Figure 1H).

claim: Cac levels are similarly distributed across AZs of type Ib and type Is inputs.
source: Cac levels are also similarly distributed across AZs of the two inputs (Figure 1I).
evidence: Supported by confocal imaging data showing distribution of normalized CacsfGFP-N intensity from single type Ib and Is AZs (Figure 1I).

claim: The relationship between VGCC levels and Pr differs between type Ib and type Is inputs.
source: These findings indicate that the relationship between VGCC levels and Pr differs between the two inputs.
evidence: Supported by functional imaging data showing significantly different slopes for the relationship between Cac levels and Pr at type Ib and Is inputs (Figure 1J).

claim: The slopes of the best-fit lines for the relationship between Cac levels and Pr at type Ib and Is inputs are significantly different.
source: Consistently, when we directly compare the best-fit lines for the relationship between Cac levels and Pr at type Ib and Is inputs from our correlative functional imaging data (Figure 1E and F), we find that the slopes are significantly different (Figure 1J).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of functional imaging data (Figure 1J).

claim: Across type Is AZs, a similar range of VGCC levels supports a higher range of release probabilities compared to type Ib AZs.
source: Across type Is AZs, a similar range of VGCC levels supports a higher range of release probabilities.
evidence: Inferred from the different slopes of the Cac-Pr relationship (Figure 1J) and similar Cac distributions (Figure 1I) between the two inputs.

claim: VGCCs can predict Pr within synaptic subtypes, but not between AZs of different synaptic subtypes.
source: Thus, VGCCs can predict Pr within synaptic subtypes, but not between AZs of different synaptic subtypes, providing a framework for understanding seemingly contradictory findings on the role of VGCCs in determining Pr.
evidence: Supported by functional imaging data showing positive correlations within inputs (Figure 1E, F) but similar overall Cac levels between inputs despite different Pr (Figure 1H).

claim: Type Is AZs experience ~twofold greater Ca2+ influx than type Ib.
source: Perhaps most notably, type Is AZs experience ~twofold greater Ca2+ influx than type Ib (He et al., 2023; Lu et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work (He et al., 2023; Lu et al., 2016).

claim: Type Ib synapses are more sensitive to the slow Ca2+ chelator EGTA than type Is synapses, indicating looser VGCC-SV coupling.
source: Using this approach, they further found that type Ib synapses are more sensitive to the slow Ca2+ chelator EGTA, indicating looser VGCC-SV coupling.
evidence: Supported by citation to prior published work (He et al., 2023).

claim: The average size of CacHaloTag-N clusters is similar at low- and high-Pr AZs.
source: We find that the average size of CacHaloTag-N clusters is similar at low- and high-Pr AZs (Figure 2F), with mean diameters of approximately 102 nm and 105 nm, respectively.
evidence: Supported by STORM imaging data showing no significant difference in CacHaloTag-N cluster area at type Ib and Is AZs (Figure 2F).

claim: The number of localizations per CacHaloTag-N cluster is similar at low- and high-Pr AZs.
source: In agreement with our confocal level data, the number of localizations per cluster was similar at low- and high-Pr AZs (Figure 2G).
evidence: Supported by STORM imaging data showing no significant difference in localizations per cluster at type Ib and Is boutons (Figure 2G).

claim: VGCCs are significantly more densely organized at high-Pr type Is AZs than low-Pr type Ib AZs.
source: We then calculated the average Cac density per AZ and found that VGCCs are significantly more densely organized at high-Pr type Is AZs than low-Pr type Ib AZs (Figure 2H, I).
evidence: Supported by STORM imaging data showing higher calculated CacHaloTag-N cluster density at type Is AZs (Figure 2H, I).

claim: Greater VGCC AZ density at type Is AZs is consistent with a recent SMLM study using antibodies to label Cac.
source: Greater VGCC AZ density at type Is AZs is consistent with a recent SMLM study using antibodies to label Cac, indicating these results are robust to different labeling approaches (Newman et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior published work (Newman et al., 2022).

claim: More compact organization of VGCCs increases their coupling to SVs and contributes to the steeper relationship between VGCC levels and Pr at high-Pr type Is AZs.
source: Together, these findings suggest that more compact organization of VGCCs increases their coupling to SVs and contributes to the steeper relationship between VGCC levels and Pr at high-Pr type Is AZs.
evidence: Inferred from STORM data showing higher VGCC density at type Is AZs (Figure 2H, I) combined with functional imaging data showing steeper Cac-Pr relationship at type Is AZs (Figure 1J).

claim: Brp/CAST/ELKS family proteins function as central organizers of both VGCCs and SV release sites at developing synapses.
source: Brp/CAST/ELKS family proteins function as central organizers of both VGCCs and SV release sites at developing synapses (Dai et al., 2006; Dong et al., 2018; Hallermann et al., 2010; Held et al., 2016; Kittel et al., 2006; Liu et al., 2014; McDonald et al., 2020; Radulovic et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work (Dai et al., 2006; Dong et al., 2018; Hallermann et al., 2010; Held et al., 2016; Kittel et al., 2006; Liu et al., 2014; McDonald et al., 2020; Radulovic et al., 2020).

claim: Brp is more densely arranged at type Is AZs as measured through SMLM and STED imaging studies.
source: Like Cac, Brp is more densely arranged at type Is AZs as measured through SMLM and stimulated emission depletion (STED) imaging studies (He et al., 2023; Jetti et al., 2023; Mrestani et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work (He et al., 2023; Jetti et al., 2023; Mrestani et al., 2021).

claim: Brp levels are lower at type Is AZs compared to type Ib AZs.
source: We simultaneously imaged type Ib and Is inputs and found lower Brp levels at type Is AZs (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: Supported by confocal imaging data showing significantly lower Brp AZ intensity at type Is terminals (Figure 3B).

claim: The Cac:Brp ratio is significantly higher at type Is synapses than type Ib synapses.
source: Since Cac levels are similar at AZs of the two inputs, lower Brp levels result in a significantly higher Cac:Brp ratio at type Is synapses, which we hypothesize promotes compact organization of VGCCs (Figure 3C).
evidence: Supported by confocal imaging data showing higher ratio of normalized CacsfGFP-N:Brp levels at type Is inputs (Figure 3C).

claim: A higher Cac:Brp ratio at type Is synapses promotes compact organization of VGCCs.
source: Since Cac levels are similar at AZs of the two inputs, lower Brp levels result in a significantly higher Cac:Brp ratio at type Is synapses, which we hypothesize promotes compact organization of VGCCs (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the observed higher Cac:Brp ratio (Figure 3C) and higher VGCC density (Figure 2H, I) at type Is AZs.

claim: Brp levels positively correlate with Pr among AZs of low-Pr type Ib inputs.
source: In contrast, we and others have previously shown that Brp levels positively correlate with Pr among AZs of low-Pr type Ib inputs (Gratz et al., 2019; Muhammad et al., 2015; Newman et al., 2017; Peled et al., 2014; Reddy-Alla et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work (Gratz et al., 2019; Muhammad et al., 2015; Newman et al., 2017; Peled et al., 2014; Reddy-Alla et al., 2017).

claim: Brp and Cac levels strongly correlate at type Ib AZs.
source: Consistently, Brp and Cac levels strongly correlate at type Ib AZs (Gratz et al., 2019) and we observe a similarly strong correlation across individual type Is AZs (Figure 3D).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work (Gratz et al., 2019) and confocal imaging data showing correlation at type Is AZs (Figure 3D).

claim: Brp and Cac levels strongly correlate at type Is AZs.
source: Consistently, Brp and Cac levels strongly correlate at type Ib AZs (Gratz et al., 2019) and we observe a similarly strong correlation across individual type Is AZs (Figure 3D).
evidence: Supported by confocal imaging data showing correlation of CacsfGFP-N and Brp at type Is single AZs (Figure 3D).

claim: Brp levels contribute in distinct ways to synaptic heterogeneity within vs. between low- and high-Pr inputs.
source: Thus, like VGCCs, Brp levels contribute in distinct ways to synaptic heterogeneity within vs. between low- and high-Pr inputs, likely due to differences in AZ organization between the two synaptic subtypes.
evidence: Inferred from data showing Brp positively correlates with Pr within inputs but is lower at high-Pr type Is inputs overall.

claim: CacsfGFP-N levels are diminished at both type Ib and Is AZs in brp null mutants.
source: CacsfGFP-N levels are diminished at both type Ib and Is AZs, demonstrating a conserved role for Brp in promoting Cac accumulation at both inputs (Figure 3G).
evidence: Supported by confocal imaging data showing reduced CacsfGFP-N normalized fluorescence intensity at type Ib and Is AZs of brp-/- NMJs (Figure 3G).

claim: Brp has a conserved role in promoting Cac accumulation at both type Ib and type Is inputs.
source: CacsfGFP-N levels are diminished at both type Ib and Is AZs, demonstrating a conserved role for Brp in promoting Cac accumulation at both inputs (Figure 3G).
evidence: Supported by confocal imaging data showing reduced CacsfGFP-N levels at both inputs in brp-/- mutants (Figure 3G).

claim: The relative decrease in Cac levels at type Ib AZs is significantly greater than at type Is AZs in brp null mutants.
source: The relative decrease in Cac levels at type Ib AZs is significantly greater than at type Is AZs, indicating a greater requirement for Brp in regulating VGCC levels at low-Pr type Ib synapses (Figure 3H).
evidence: Supported by confocal imaging data showing ratio of CacsfGFP-N fluorescence intensity at type Ib and Is AZs between brp-/- and control NMJs (Figure 3H).

claim: There is a greater requirement for Brp in regulating VGCC levels at low-Pr type Ib synapses compared to high-Pr type Is synapses.
source: The relative decrease in Cac levels at type Ib AZs is significantly greater than at type Is AZs, indicating a greater requirement for Brp in regulating VGCC levels at low-Pr type Ib synapses (Figure 3H).
evidence: Inferred from the greater relative decrease in Cac levels at type Ib AZs in brp-/- mutants (Figure 3H).

claim: An additional factor or factors function with or upstream of Brp to establish differences in Brp dependence at low- and high-Pr AZs.
source: This suggests that an additional factor or factors function with or upstream of Brp to establish differences in Brp dependence at low- and high-Pr AZs.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observed differential requirement for Brp at the two inputs (Figure 3H).

claim: Drosophila motor neurons homeostatically increase neurotransmitter release to maintain synaptic communication in response to acute or chronic inhibition of glutamate receptors at NMJs.
source: In response to acute or chronic inhibition of glutamate receptors at NMJs, Drosophila motor neurons homeostatically increase neurotransmitter release to maintain synaptic communication (Davis and Müller, 2015; Frank, 2014; James et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work (Davis and Müller, 2015; Frank, 2014; James et al., 2019).

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of glutamate receptors with Philanthotoxin-433 (PhTx) induces acute presynaptic homeostatic potentiation of release (PHP) within minutes.
source: Pharmacological inhibition of glutamate receptors with the wasp toxin Philanthotoxin-433 (PhTx) induces acute presynaptic homeostatic potentiation of release (PHP) within minutes (Frank et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior published work (Frank et al., 2006).

claim: Acute PHP involves rapid changes in VGCC and other AZ protein levels at type Ib AZs.
source: We and others have demonstrated that acute PHP involves rapid changes in VGCC and other AZ protein levels at type Ib AZs (Böhme et al., 2019; Gratz et al., 2019; Weyhersmüller et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work (Böhme et al., 2019; Gratz et al., 2019; Weyhersmüller et al., 2011).

claim: PhTx induces acute PHP at both type Ib and Is synapses.
source: PhTx induces acute PHP at both type Ib and Is synapses (Genç and Davis, 2019), but the molecular changes underlying PHP at high-Pr type Is AZs remain unknown.
evidence: Supported by citation to prior published work (Genç and Davis, 2019).

claim: PhTx treatment induces a significant increase in Brp levels at type Is AZs.
source: We observe a significant PhTx-induced increase in Brp and CacsfGFP-N levels at type Is AZs similar to type Ib (Figure 4C and D; Gratz et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by confocal imaging data showing increased Brp fluorescence intensity at PhTx-treated type Is terminals (Figure 4C).

claim: PhTx treatment induces a significant increase in CacsfGFP-N levels at type Is AZs.
source: We observe a significant PhTx-induced increase in Brp and CacsfGFP-N levels at type Is AZs similar to type Ib (Figure 4C and D; Gratz et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by confocal imaging data showing increased CacsfGFP-N fluorescence intensity at PhTx-treated type Is terminals (Figure 4D).

claim: PhTx-induced potentiation of neurotransmitter release involves the rapid accumulation of VGCCs at both low- and high-Pr AZs.
source: Thus, despite their distinct baseline transmission and organizational properties, PhTx-induced potentiation of neurotransmitter release involves the rapid accumulation of VGCCs at both low- and high-Pr AZs.
evidence: Supported by confocal imaging data showing increased CacsfGFP-N levels at both type Ib and Is AZs following PhTx treatment (Figure 4D).

claim: At low-Pr type Ib AZs, Brp is a critical regulator of PHP-induced accumulation of proteins associated with SV priming and release, specifically Unc13A and Syntaxin-1A.
source: At low-Pr type Ib AZs, Brp is a critical regulator of PHP-induced accumulation of proteins associated with SV priming and release, specifically Unc13A and Syntaxin-1A (Böhme et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior published work (Böhme et al., 2019).

claim: At type Ib AZs, PhTx induces a Brp-dependent increase in Cac density and decrease in channel mobility.
source: At type Ib AZs, PhTx also induces a Brp-dependent increase in Cac density and decrease in channel mobility (Ghelani et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior published work (Ghelani et al., 2023).

claim: Brp itself becomes more densely organized during PHP.
source: Notably, Brp itself becomes more densely organized during PHP (Ghelani et al., 2023), consistent with its denser organization at high-Pr type Is AZs (Mrestani et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work (Ghelani et al., 2023; Mrestani et al., 2021).

claim: PhTx failed to induce accumulation of Cac at either type Ib or Is AZs in brp-/- mutants.
source: We find that PhTx failed to induce accumulation of Cac at either type Ib or Is AZs in brp-/- mutants, demonstrating a shared requirement for Brp in regulating VGCC dynamics at both inputs (Figure 4G).
evidence: Supported by confocal imaging data showing no significant increase in CacsfGFP-N fluorescence intensity at PhTx-treated cacsfGFP-N;brp-/- type Ib terminals (Figure 4G).

claim: There is a shared requirement for Brp in regulating VGCC dynamics at both type Ib and type Is inputs during PHP.
source: We find that PhTx failed to induce accumulation of Cac at either type Ib or Is AZs in brp-/- mutants, demonstrating a shared requirement for Brp in regulating VGCC dynamics at both inputs (Figure 4G).
evidence: Supported by confocal imaging data showing no PhTx-induced increase in CacsfGFP-N levels at either input in brp-/- mutants (Figure 4G).

claim: CacsfGFP-N levels are significantly decreased at type Is AZs in brp-/- mutants following PhTx treatment.
source: In contrast to no change at type Ib AZs, CacsfGFP-N levels are significantly decreased at type Is AZs (Figure 4G), revealing an input-specific role for Brp in maintaining VGCC levels during the dynamic reorganization of AZs.
evidence: Supported by confocal imaging data showing decreased CacsfGFP-N fluorescence intensity at PhTx-treated cacsfGFP-N;brp-/- type Is terminals (Figure 4G).

claim: Brp has an input-specific role in maintaining VGCC levels during the dynamic reorganization of AZs.
source: In contrast to no change at type Ib AZs, CacsfGFP-N levels are significantly decreased at type Is AZs (Figure 4G), revealing an input-specific role for Brp in maintaining VGCC levels during the dynamic reorganization of AZs.
evidence: Inferred from the differential effect of PhTx on Cac levels at type Ib vs. Is AZs in brp-/- mutants (Figure 4G).

claim: PhTx induces a decrease in Cac mobility at wild-type type Ib AZs.
source: Consistently, Ghelani et al., 2023 found that whereas PhTx induces a decrease in Cac mobility at wild-type type Ib AZs, in brp-/- mutants Cac mobility increases (Ghelani et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior published work (Ghelani et al., 2023).

claim: In brp-/- mutants, PhTx treatment causes Cac mobility to increase at type Ib AZs.
source: Consistently, Ghelani et al., 2023 found that whereas PhTx induces a decrease in Cac mobility at wild-type type Ib AZs, in brp-/- mutants Cac mobility increases (Ghelani et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior published work (Ghelani et al., 2023).

claim: Potentiating synapses must coordinate the accumulation of new VGCCs with the stabilization of existing channels.
source: Together, these findings suggest potentiating synapses must coordinate the accumulation of new VGCCs with the stabilization of existing channels, and that meeting this challenge is more dependent upon Brp at high-Pr AZs.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observed differential effects of brp loss on Cac levels during PHP at the two inputs (Figure 4G).

claim: Meeting the challenge of coordinating VGCC accumulation and stabilization during potentiation is more dependent upon Brp at high-Pr AZs.
source: Together, these findings suggest potentiating synapses must coordinate the accumulation of new VGCCs with the stabilization of existing channels, and that meeting this challenge is more dependent upon Brp at high-Pr AZs.
evidence: Inferred from the greater impact of brp loss on Cac levels at type Is AZs during PHP (Figure 4G).

claim: VGCC auxiliary α2δ and β subunits regulate forward channel trafficking, membrane insertion, and function.
source: In addition to the pore-forming α subunits, VGCCs comprise auxiliary α2δ and β subunits that regulate forward channel trafficking, membrane insertion, and function (Figure 5A; Campiglio and Flucher, 2015; Dolphin and Lee, 2020; Weiss and Zamponi, 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work (Campiglio and Flucher, 2015; Dolphin and Lee, 2020; Weiss and Zamponi, 2017).

claim: β subunits interact with pore-forming α subunits intracellularly.
source: β subunits interact with pore-forming α subunits intracellularly, whereas GPI-anchored α2δ subunits are largely extracellular.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about VGCC structure.

claim: GPI-anchored α2δ subunits are largely extracellular.
source: β subunits interact with pore-forming α subunits intracellularly, whereas GPI-anchored α2δ subunits are largely extracellular.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about VGCC structure.

claim: α2δ subunits have been shown to interact with a growing number of extracellular proteins to promote synaptogenesis.
source: Beyond their interaction with α subunits, α2δs have been shown to interact with a growing number of extracellular proteins to promote synaptogenesis (Bauer et al., 2010; Dolphin, 2018; Risher et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work (Bauer et al., 2010; Dolphin, 2018; Risher et al., 2018).

claim: The Drosophila genome encodes one synaptic Cav2 α subunit (Cac), one β subunit, and three α2δ subunits.
source: The Drosophila genome encodes one synaptic Cav2 α subunit (Cac), one β subunit, and three α2δ subunits (Littleton and Ganetzky, 2000).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior published work (Littleton and Ganetzky, 2000).

claim: Ca-β encodes the sole Drosophila β subunit.
source: Ca-β encodes the sole Drosophila β subunit and has been shown to enhance Ca2+ transients in sensory neurons (Kanamori et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior published work (Kanamori et al., 2013).

claim: Ca-β has been shown to enhance Ca2+ transients in sensory neurons.
source: Ca-β encodes the sole Drosophila β subunit and has been shown to enhance Ca2+ transients in sensory neurons (Kanamori et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior published work (Kanamori et al., 2013).

claim: Drosophila α2δ–3, also known as Straightjacket (Stj), has well-characterized roles at the NMJ in promoting Ca2+ channel clustering, homeostatic plasticity, and synapse formation and organization.
source: Drosophila α2δ–3, also known as Straightjacket (Stj), has well-characterized roles at the NMJ in promoting Ca2+ channel clustering, homeostatic plasticity, and, independently of Cac, synapse formation and organization (Dickman et al., 2008; Hoover et al., 2019; Kurshan et al., 2009; Ly et al., 2008; Schöpf et al., 2021; Wang et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work (Dickman et al., 2008; Hoover et al., 2019; Kurshan et al., 2009; Ly et al., 2008; Schöpf et al., 2021; Wang et al., 2016).

claim: Stolid was recently shown to promote dendritic Cac expression in motor neurons.
source: Stolid was recently shown to promote dendritic Cac expression in motor neurons, whereas Ma2d is known to function in muscle where it is broadly expressed (Heinrich and Ryglewski, 2020; Reuveny et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior published work (Heinrich and Ryglewski, 2020).

claim: Ma2d is known to function in muscle where it is broadly expressed.
source: Stolid was recently shown to promote dendritic Cac expression in motor neurons, whereas Ma2d is known to function in muscle where it is broadly expressed (Heinrich and Ryglewski, 2020; Reuveny et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior published work (Reuveny et al., 2018).

claim: All endogenously tagged VGCC auxiliary subunits (Ca-β, Stj, Stolid) are expressed in the synaptic neuropil of the larval ventral ganglion in a pattern similar to Cac.
source: We investigated the expression of each endogenously tagged subunit in the larval ventral ganglion and found that all subunits are expressed in the synaptic neuropil in a pattern similar to the α subunit Cac (Figure 5F–H; Gratz et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by confocal imaging data showing expression patterns in the ventral ganglion (Figure 5F-H).

claim: Ca-βV5-C is highly enriched in the mushroom bodies of the larval brain, similar to Cac.
source: Similar to Cac, Ca-βV5-C is highly enriched in the mushroom bodies of the larval brain.
evidence: Supported by confocal imaging data (Figure 5F) and comparison to prior work on Cac (Gratz et al., 2019).

claim: Only Ca-βV5-C and StjV5-N are present at the larval NMJ.
source: We next investigated expression at the larval NMJ where Cac localizes in a single punctum at each AZ and found that only Ca-βV5-C and StjV5-N are present (Figure 5F–H).
evidence: Supported by confocal imaging data showing Ca-β and Stj expression at NMJs but not Stolid (Figure 5F-H).

claim: Stolid does not play a role in regulating Ca2+ transients at the larval NMJ.
source: This aligns with the recent finding that Stolid does not play a role in regulating Ca2+ transients at the larval NMJ (Heinrich and Ryglewski, 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior published work (Heinrich and Ryglewski, 2020).

claim: Ca-βV5-C is expressed in muscle.
source: We also observe Ca-βV5-C expression in muscle as expected for the sole Drosophila β subunit (Figure 5F and see Figure 6C).
evidence: Supported by confocal imaging data (Figure 5F, Figure 6C).

claim: Both Ca-βV5-C and StjV5-N localize to AZs.
source: To investigate Ca-βV5-C and StjV5-N localization at type Ib and Is AZs, we used super-resolution optical reassignment microscopy. Both subunits localize to AZs labeled with Cac or the CAST/ELKS AZ cytomatrix protein Brp (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: Supported by super-resolution imaging data showing colocalization with Brp and Cac (Figure 6A, B).

claim: Brp rings surround puncta of VGCCs including Ca-βV5-C.
source: We observe Brp rings surrounding puncta of VGCCs including Ca-βV5-C (Figure 6A).
evidence: Supported by super-resolution imaging data (Figure 6A).

claim: Ca-βV5-C levels are similar at type Ib and Is AZs.
source: As predicted, we found that Ca-βV5-C levels are similar at type Ib and Is AZs (Figure 6E).
evidence: Supported by confocal imaging data showing no significant difference in Ca-βV5-C fluorescence intensity at type Ib and Is AZs (Figure 6E).

claim: StjV5-N levels are significantly lower at high-Pr type Is AZs compared to type Ib AZs.
source: In contrast, StjV5-N levels are significantly lower at high-Pr type Is AZs (Figure 6F).
evidence: Supported by confocal imaging data showing lower StjV5-N fluorescence intensity at type Is AZs (Figure 6F).

claim: While Cac and Ca-β are present in similar ratios at AZs of both inputs, the same is not true of Stj/α2δ–3 with high-Pr type Is AZs exhibiting lower levels of Stj.
source: Thus, while Cac and Ca-β are present in similar ratios at AZs of both inputs, surprisingly, the same is not true of Stj/α2δ–3 with high-Pr type Is AZs exhibiting lower levels of Stj.
evidence: Inferred from data showing similar Cac and Ca-β levels at both inputs (Figure 1H, 6E) but lower Stj levels at type Is AZs (Figure 6F).

claim: α:α2δ–3 stoichiometry is not always 1:1 in vivo and differs at low- and high-Pr synapses.
source: This unexpected finding indicates that α:α2δ–3 stoichiometry is not always 1:1 in vivo and differs at low- and high-Pr synapses.
evidence: Inferred from data showing similar Cac levels but different Stj levels at the two inputs (Figure 1H, 6F).

claim: α2δ interactions with α subunits may be transient, leading to a pool of VGCCs lacking α2δ.
source: This is consistent with studies of mammalian subunits indicating that in contrast to β subunits, α2δ interactions with α subunits may be transient, leading to a pool of VGCCs lacking α2δ (Müller et al., 2010; Voigt et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work (Müller et al., 2010; Voigt et al., 2016).

claim: There may be a pool of VGCCs lacking an α2δ subunit at endogenous synapses that is specific to or enriched at high-Pr type Is AZs.
source: Our results indicate this pool may be present in vivo and larger at high-Pr type Is inputs.
evidence: Inferred from data showing lower Stj levels at type Is AZs despite similar Cac levels (Figure 1H, 6F).

claim: StjV5-N and CacsfGFP-N levels are highly positively correlated at type Is AZs.
source: To further investigate the contribution of Stj to synaptic heterogeneity, we analyzed the relationship between Cac and Stj levels at individual AZs of type Is inputs. StjV5-N and CacsfGFP-N levels are highly positively correlated at type Is AZs (Figure 6G).
evidence: Supported by confocal imaging data showing correlation of CacsfGFP-N and StjV5-N fluorescence intensity levels at type Is single AZs (Figure 6G).

claim: StjV5-N and CacsfGFP-N levels are highly positively correlated at type Ib AZs.
source: We observe the same relationship between StjV5-N and CacsfGFP-N levels at type Ib AZs (Figure 6H).
evidence: Supported by confocal imaging data showing correlation of CacsfGFP-N and StjV5-N fluorescence intensity levels at type Ib single AZs (Figure 6H).

claim: Stj levels are positively correlated with Pr within, but not between, inputs.
source: Because Pr is highly positively correlated with Cac levels within synaptic subtypes, this indicates that Stj levels are also positively correlated with Pr within, but not between, inputs.
evidence: Inferred from the positive correlation between Stj and Cac at individual AZs (Figure 6G, H) combined with the positive correlation between Cac and Pr within inputs (Figure 1E, F) and lower Stj at high-Pr type Is inputs (Figure 6F).

claim: Overexpression of α2δ subunits increases α subunit abundance in flies and mammals.
source: In flies and mammals, overexpression of α2δ subunits increases α subunit abundance, whereas overexpression of the α subunit alone does not (Cao et al., 2004; Cunningham et al., 2022; Hoppa et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work (Cao et al., 2004; Cunningham et al., 2022; Hoppa et al., 2012).

claim: Overexpression of the α subunit alone does not increase α subunit abundance.
source: In flies and mammals, overexpression of α2δ subunits increases α subunit abundance, whereas overexpression of the α subunit alone does not (Cao et al., 2004; Cunningham et al., 2022; Hoppa et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work (Cao et al., 2004; Cunningham et al., 2022; Hoppa et al., 2012).

claim: Following PhTx exposure, StjV5-N is recruited on a rapid timescale to both low- and high-Pr AZs, increasing by a similar percentage at both type Ib and Is AZs (27% and 26%, respectively).
source: Following PhTx exposure, we find that StjV5-N is recruited on a rapid timescale to both low- and high-Pr AZs, increasing by a similar percentage at both type Ib and Is AZs (27% and 26%, respectively) as predicted (Figure 7A-C).
evidence: Supported by confocal imaging data showing increased StjV5-N fluorescence intensity at PhTx-treated type Ib and Is terminals (Figure 7C).

claim: Cac levels increase by 33% at type Ib and 30% at type Is AZs following PhTx treatment.
source: Cac levels are similarly increased (33% at type Ib and 30% at type Is; See Figure 4D), suggesting coordinated regulation.
evidence: Supported by confocal imaging data (Figure 4D).

claim: The similar increases in Cac and Stj levels during PHP suggest coordinated regulation.
source: Cac levels are similarly increased (33% at type Ib and 30% at type Is; See Figure 4D), suggesting coordinated regulation.
evidence: Inferred from the similar percentage increases in Cac and Stj levels following PhTx treatment.

claim: Cac abundance is increased in chronic PHP, which is induced by genetic loss of the GluRIIA receptor subunit.
source: We have previously shown that Cac abundance is also increased in chronic PHP, which is induced by genetic loss of the GluRIIA receptor subunit (Gratz et al., 2019; Li et al., 2018; Petersen et al., 1997).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work (Gratz et al., 2019; Li et al., 2018; Petersen et al., 1997).

claim: StjV5-N levels are elevated at AZs of both type Ib and Is inputs in GluRIIA-/- null animals (18% and 17%, respectively).
source: We investigated Stj dynamics in GluRIIA-/- null animals and observed elevated StjV5-N levels at AZs of both type Ib and Is inputs (18% and 17%, respectively; Figure 7D–F), indicating similar dynamics during chronic PHP.
evidence: Supported by confocal imaging data showing increased StjV5-N fluorescence intensity levels at stjV5-N;GluRIIA-/- type Ib and Is terminals (Figure 7F).

claim: Stj is required for the accumulation of Cac at type Ib AZs during both acute and chronic PHP.
source: These data are consistent with the recent finding that in addition to its previously uncovered role in promoting an increase in the readily releasable pool of SVs (Wang et al., 2016), Stj is required for the accumulation of Cac at type Ib AZs during both acute and chronic PHP (Zhang et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work (Wang et al., 2016; Zhang et al., 2023).

claim: The abundance of multiple key AZ proteins distinguishes low- and high-Pr synapses within, but not between, inputs at baseline and during homeostatic plasticity.
source: Thus, the abundance of multiple key AZ proteins distinguishes low- and high-Pr synapses within, but not between, inputs at baseline and during homeostatic plasticity.
evidence: Inferred from data showing that Cac, Brp, and Stj levels correlate with Pr within inputs but show different patterns between inputs, both at baseline and during PHP.

claim: Two broad intersecting mechanisms contribute to synaptic diversity: (1) nanoscale spatial organization and relative molecular content establish distinct average basal release probabilities that differ between inputs and (2) coordinated modulation of VGCC and active zone protein abundance independently tunes Pr among individual synapses of distinct inputs.
source: Our findings suggest a model in which two broad intersecting mechanisms contribute to synaptic diversity in the nervous system: (1) nanoscale spatial organization and relative molecular content establish distinct average basal release probabilities that differ between inputs and (2) coordinated modulation of VGCC and active zone protein abundance independently tunes Pr among individual synapses of distinct inputs.
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the collective findings of the study.

claim: VGCC number positively correlates with Pr among mature synapses in the hippocampus.
source: This holds true among mature synapses in the hippocampus or immature synapses of the calyx of Held (Holderith et al., 2012; Sheng et al., 2012) and at the developing Drosophila NMJ where the differences in Pr and channel number between AZs of a single input also correlate with synapse maturity (Akbergenova et al., 2018; Gratz et al., 2019; Newman et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work (Holderith et al., 2012; Sheng et al., 2012).

claim: VGCC number positively correlates with Pr among immature synapses of the calyx of Held.
source: This holds true among mature synapses in the hippocampus or immature synapses of the calyx of Held (Holderith et al., 2012; Sheng et al., 2012) and at the developing Drosophila NMJ where the differences in Pr and channel number between AZs of a single input also correlate with synapse maturity (Akbergenova et al., 2018; Gratz et al., 2019; Newman et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work (Holderith et al., 2012; Sheng et al., 2012).

claim: At the developing Drosophila NMJ, differences in Pr and channel number between AZs of a single input correlate with synapse maturity.
source: This holds true among mature synapses in the hippocampus or immature synapses of the calyx of Held (Holderith et al., 2012; Sheng et al., 2012) and at the developing Drosophila NMJ where the differences in Pr and channel number between AZs of a single input also correlate with synapse maturity (Akbergenova et al., 2018; Gratz et al., 2019; Newman et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work (Akbergenova et al., 2018; Gratz et al., 2019; Newman et al., 2022).

claim: The mature calyx of Held has higher Pr yet recruits fewer Ca2+ channels compared to the immature calyx.
source: Although the number of functional VGCCs positively correlates with Pr among synapses in the immature calyx of Held, the mature calyx has higher Pr yet recruits fewer Ca2+ channels (Fedchyshyn and Wang, 2005; Sheng et al., 2012; Wang and Augustine, 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work (Fedchyshyn and Wang, 2005; Sheng et al., 2012; Wang and Augustine, 2014).

claim: In the cerebellum, inhibitory stellate cells form high-Pr synapses with lower VGCC levels than low-Pr synapses formed by excitatory granular cells.
source: Similarly, in the cerebellum, inhibitory stellate cells form high-Pr synapses with lower VGCC levels than low-Pr synapses formed by excitatory granular cells (Rebola et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior published work (Rebola et al., 2019).

claim: At distinct inputs formed by CA1 pyramidal neurons, Ca2+ influx is greater at high-Pr synapses, but raising Ca2+ entry at low-Pr synapses to high-Pr synapse levels was not sufficient to increase synaptic strength to high-Pr input levels.
source: At distinct inputs formed by CA1 pyramidal neurons, Ca2+ influx is greater at high-Pr synapses, but doesn't explain differences in synaptic strength as raising Ca2+ entry at low-Pr synapses to high-Pr synapse levels was not sufficient to increase synaptic strength to high-Pr input levels (Aldahabi et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior published work (Aldahabi et al., 2022).

claim: In CA1 pyramidal neurons, differences in Munc-13-dependent SV priming are proposed to establish synapse-specific release properties, possibly due to the presence of distinct isoforms at low- vs. high-Pr connections.
source: In CA1 pyramidal neurons, differences in Munc-13-dependent SV priming are proposed to establish synapse-specific release properties, possibly due to the presence of distinct isoforms at low- vs. high-Pr connections.
evidence: This is a proposal from prior work cited in the discussion (Aldahabi et al., 2022).

claim: Fewer VGCCs are more tightly coupled to SVs at high-Pr stellate synapses in the cerebellum.
source: In the cerebellum, fewer VGCC are more tightly coupled to SVs at high-Pr stellate synapses (Rebola et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior published work (Rebola et al., 2019).

claim: More densely organized VGCCs at the mature vs. developing calyx of Held exhibit greater coupling with SVs.
source: More densely organized VGCCs at the mature vs. developing calyx of Held also exhibit greater coupling with SVs (Chen et al., 2015; Fedchyshyn and Wang, 2005; Fekete et al., 2019; Nakamura et al., 2015; Sheng et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work (Chen et al., 2015; Fedchyshyn and Wang, 2005; Fekete et al., 2019; Nakamura et al., 2015; Sheng et al., 2012).

claim: Brp interacts broadly with AZ proteins to promote Cac clustering, organize SVs, and recruit Unc13A, which defines SV release sites.
source: Brp interacts broadly with AZ proteins to promote Cac clustering, organize SVs, and recruit Unc13A, which defines SV release sites (Böhme et al., 2016; Fulterer et al., 2018; Ghelani et al., 2023; Liu et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work (Böhme et al., 2016; Fulterer et al., 2018; Ghelani et al., 2023; Liu et al., 2011).

claim: Type Ib and Is synapses have distinct requirements for Brp during synapse formation and homeostatic potentiation.
source: While Brp clearly plays a central role in AZ organization and reorganization, we also find that type Ib and Is synapses have distinct requirements for Brp during synapse formation and homeostatic potentiation (Figures 3 and 4).
evidence: Supported by data showing differential effects of brp loss at the two inputs (Figures 3, 4).

claim: Synapse-specific roles for Brp are supported by a recent functional imaging study in Drosophila.
source: Synapse-specific roles for Brp are supported by a recent functional imaging study in Drosophila (Jetti et al., 2023) and studies of ELKS at mammalian inhibitory and excitatory synapses (Held et al., 2016), and suggest additional factors establish neuron-specific differences in Brp dependence.
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work (Jetti et al., 2023; Held et al., 2016).

claim: Studies of ELKS at mammalian inhibitory and excitatory synapses support synapse-specific roles for CAST/ELKS proteins.
source: Synapse-specific roles for Brp are supported by a recent functional imaging study in Drosophila (Jetti et al., 2023) and studies of ELKS at mammalian inhibitory and excitatory synapses (Held et al., 2016), and suggest additional factors establish neuron-specific differences in Brp dependence.
evidence: Supported by citation to prior published work (Held et al., 2016).

claim: A recent single-cell transcriptomic study of type Ib and Is motor neurons provides an unbiased starting point for identifying candidate regulators of molecular differences at low- and high-Pr AZs.
source: A recent single-cell transcriptomic study of type Ib and Is motor neurons provides an unbiased starting point for identifying candidate regulators of molecular differences at low- and high-Pr AZs (Jetti et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior published work (Jetti et al., 2023).

claim: Many genes encoding VGCC subunits across species are extensively alternatively spliced to generate additional functional diversity.
source: In addition to the ability to mix and match subunits, many of the genes encoding VGCC subunits across species are extensively alternatively spliced to generate additional functional diversity (Cingolani et al., 2023; Lipscombe et al., 2013; Lipscombe and Lopez Soto, 2019) – an area of great interest for further investigation at the Drosophila NMJ.
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work (Cingolani et al., 2023; Lipscombe et al., 2013; Lipscombe and Lopez Soto, 2019).

claim: Both β and α2δ subunits are generally considered positive regulators of channel trafficking and function.
source: Because both β and α2δ subunits are generally considered positive regulators of channel trafficking and function, we were surprised to find upon endogenously tagging Stj/α2δ–3 that its levels are lower at high-Pr AZs (Figures 5 and 6).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about VGCC auxiliary subunits.

claim: A single-molecule tracking and modeling study of mammalian VGCCs found that α2δ subunits have a relatively low affinity for α subunits and predicted a population of α subunits not associated with an α2δ subunit.
source: While some previous studies have observed a tight association between the two subunits, a single-molecule tracking and modeling study of mammalian VGCCs found that α2δ subunits have a relatively low affinity for α subunits and predicted a population of α subunits not associated with an α2δ subunit (Cassidy et al., 2014; Voigt et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work (Cassidy et al., 2014; Voigt et al., 2016).

claim: α and β subunits were isolated at near equimolar ratios following affinity purification of Cav2 channels, whereas molar levels of α2δ were 90% lower.
source: Consistently, whereas α and β subunits were isolated at near equimolar ratios following affinity purification of Cav2 channels, molar levels of α2δ were a surprising 90% lower (Müller et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior published work (Müller et al., 2010).

claim: Stj is both required and rate limiting for Cac accumulation at AZs.
source: Stj is both required (Dickman et al., 2008; Kurshan et al., 2009; Ly et al., 2008) and rate limiting (Cunningham et al., 2022) for Cac accumulation at AZs.
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work (Dickman et al., 2008; Kurshan et al., 2009; Ly et al., 2008; Cunningham et al., 2022).

claim: Stj does not appear to function in the stabilization of channels at the AZ membrane, but rather at an upstream step in the progression from ER to plasma membrane.
source: Stj does not appear to function in the stabilization of channels at the AZ membrane, but rather at an upstream step in the progression from ER to plasma membrane (Cunningham et al., 2022), so complexes may not need to be maintained.
evidence: Supported by citation to prior published work (Cunningham et al., 2022).

claim: A recent study in C. elegans suggested that auxiliary subunits promote stabilization of VGCCs in the membrane.
source: However, a recent study in C. elegans suggested that auxiliary subunits to promote stabilization in the membrane, raising the possibility that the difference observed in α2δ levels could translate to a difference in α subunit mobility within Ib vs. Is AZs (Oh et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior published work (Oh et al., 2023).

claim: In mammals, α-Neurexin specifically inhibits Ca2+ currents in Cav2.2 channels containing α2δ–3.
source: In mammals, α-Neurexin specifically inhibits Ca2+ currents in Cav2.2 channels containing α2δ–3 (Tong et al., 2017), which, if similar at the Drosophila NMJ, could result in greater inhibition of channel function at type Ib AZs and contribute to the observed difference in Ca2+ influx.
evidence: Supported by citation to prior published work (Tong et al., 2017).

claim: Loss of Drosophila Neurexin reduces neurotransmitter release at the NMJ.
source: Loss of Drosophila Neurexin reduces neurotransmitter release at the NMJ, but it also leads to reduced synaptogenesis so whether this is a direct effect remains unknown (He et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior published work (He et al., 2007).

claim: A recent transcriptomic study observed no significant differences in mRNA splice isoforms of Stj between type Ib and Is motor neurons.
source: A recent transcriptomic study observed no significant differences in mRNA splice isoforms, but transcript levels do not always reflect protein levels (Jetti et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior published work (Jetti et al., 2023).

claim: Cac and Stj levels increase by similar amounts at type Ib and type Is inputs during PHP, suggesting the difference in stoichiometry is maintained following homeostatic potentiation.
source: Cac and Stj levels increase by similar amounts at the two inputs, suggesting the difference in stoichiometry is maintained following homeostatic potentiation.
evidence: Inferred from data showing similar percentage increases in Cac and Stj at both inputs during PHP (Figures 4D, 7C).

claim: α2δ–3 is an important drug target for treating epilepsy, neuropathic pain, and anxiety.
source: α2δ–3 is an important drug target for treating epilepsy, neuropathic pain, and anxiety, so understanding its cell-specific roles and how α:α2δ–3 stoichiometry impacts channel function and contributes to synaptic diversity is of great interest.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the clinical relevance of α2δ subunits.
